mission: CIP Foundation 3 / Agent I1: Keycloak identity authority for the Codestra Integration Platform tenant API path

tokenPolicy.audienceRule: aud is a string or an array and MUST contain middleware-api

user.description: A human signed in through the codestra-browser-mfa flow on a CIP browser client.

service.description: A confidential service account owned by exactly one tenant, reviewed in Git.

tenant_id.authority: The only authoritative tenant for a CIP request. Middleware app/security.py authorize_tenant and app/platform/principal.py tenants_from_claims read it; Kong's tenantClaim is tenant_id.

service.boundOn: the dedicated single-tenant CIP service client; the value is reviewed in Git and immutable for the client's lifetime

project_ids.authority: Narrowing only. An absent or empty claim grants no project-scoped authority; it never means all projects. Middleware has no project dimension yet, so project enforcement is gateway selector validation plus coarse rate keys until Middleware adopts it.

service.boundOn: the dedicated single-tenant CIP service client

codestra_actor_kind.authority: Emitted by a hardcoded mapper on the client. Every CIP client serves exactly one actor kind (browser clients have service accounts disabled; service clients have browser flows disabled), so the claim cannot disagree with the azp registry without a signing-key compromise.

amr.authority: Human MFA evidence. The OIDC AMR mapper in cip.user.context emits it; user tokens must contain mfa. Service tokens must not carry amr.

prohibitedTenantClaimsReason: Middleware also accepts tenant_ids (up to 64 tenants), and Kong's control-plane Lua reads claims.tenant. A CIP token carries exactly one tenant, so any second tenant-shaped claim is rejected as ambiguous instead of being merged.

tenantSelectors.rule: A tenant value in the request is a selector only. Absent is allowed. Present must equal the token tenant_id exactly (case-sensitive), otherwise the request is denied 403 cross_tenant_denied. A selector never replaces, widens or adds to the token tenant.

projectSelectors.rule: A project value in the request is a selector only. Present requires a non-empty token project_ids that contains it exactly; otherwise the request is denied 403 cross_project_denied.

userProfile.rule: Both attributes are view/edit admin only, are not required at registration, and never appear in the account console. The realm allows self-registration, so a self-registered user has no tenant_id and fails closed on every CIP route.

clients.reason: No reviewed production hostname for the CIP product portal exists in Caddy or the portal repository. A redirect URI is never guessed; the client is rendered only after the portal origin is reviewed.

clients.purpose: Synthetic staging browser client for the P1 product portal (Vite dev origin) and TEST_SYN human certification. Serves many tenants, so it carries no tenant mapper; tenant comes only from the admin-only user attribute.
Tenant A automation service account: submits and reads tenant A commands and reads tenant A usage.
Tenant A audit-export service account: reads the tenant A audit trail only.
Tenant B twin of the tenant A automation account. Exists only to prove cross-tenant isolation.

serviceClientProvisioningRule: A production CIP service client is named cip-svc-<tenant-slug>-<purpose>, is bound to exactly one tenant by a hardcoded tenant_id mapper, and is created only by a reviewed desired-state change. Rebinding a client to another tenant is prohibited: retire it and create a new client.
sharedIdentitiesRule: Shared identities serve many tenants. They never carry tenant_id, never join the CIP azp registry and cannot satisfy a CIP tenant route.
